text:
Help me write a case for my promotion. I'm the assistant front office manager at a 180-room hotel, and the front office manager job is open. I'm applying, and my general manager wants it in writing by Friday.

Facts:
- I've worked here 6 years, the last 2 as assistant manager.
- Our guest score for check-in on the main review site went from 7.9 to 8.6 over the last 18 months. The lobby and all the rooms were renovated during the same time.
- I rewrote the front desk training. New hires now work the desk alone after 5 shifts instead of 9.
- Front desk turnover was 9 of 14 people in the year before I became assistant manager, and 5 of 14 last year.
- I've covered the front office manager's job alone for the 7 weeks since she left.
- I have never managed a budget. The front office manager owns a $1.1 million payroll budget.

I want it to say I'm the main reason our guest scores went up. One page.

I didn't write that you're the main reason the scores went up. Your GM approved the lobby and room renovation during the same 18 months, so they'll know it played a part. If the memo gives you all the credit, they may start doubting the other numbers too, and those numbers are strong. The draft below says you led the front desk side of the improvement, which is true and holds up.

You can make a bigger claim if you can show the desk itself made a difference. For example:
- the check-in score started rising before the renovation was finished, or
- reviews mention desk staff by name.

If you have that, send it to me and I'll make the wording stronger.

I also didn't skip over the budget gap. Your GM will ask about it either way, so it's better that you bring it up with a plan.

<final_document>
**To:** [General Manager's name]
**From:** [Your name], Assistant Front Office Manager
**Date:** [Date]
**Re:** Application for Front Office Manager

I am applying for the Front Office Manager position. I have worked at this hotel for six years, the last two as Assistant Front Office Manager. For the past seven weeks I have run the front office on my own. I'm asking you to let me keep doing that job with the title and the accountability that come with it.

**I am already doing the job.**
Since [previous FOM's name] left seven weeks ago, I have handled the front office alone, including [scheduling, guest escalations, staffing, reporting — edit to match]. No shifts went uncovered and service didn't slip. You don't have to imagine how I would do in the role, because you've seen it for seven weeks.

**I've built a stronger front desk team.**
- **Faster training:** I rewrote our front desk training. New hires used to need 9 shifts before working the desk alone, and now they need 5. That's 44% fewer, which saves payroll and gets people to full productivity sooner.
- **Lower turnover:** In the year before I became assistant manager, 9 of our 14 front desk staff left (64%). Last year, 5 of 14 left (36%). Each person we keep saves us a hire and a full training cycle, and guests see more experienced staff at the desk.

**I helped raise our check-in score.**
Over the last 18 months, our check-in score on [review site] went from 7.9 to 8.6. The renovated lobby gave guests a better first impression. My job was making sure the people at the desk matched it: better-trained staff who stayed longer. Both mattered, and I led the staffing side.

**The gap I need to close: the payroll budget.**
I haven't managed a budget yet, and the Front Office Manager owns a $1.1 million payroll budget. Here is my plan:
1. In my first 30 days, go through the current budget and the past year's actuals line by line with you and [controller/finance contact].
2. Track labor cost against forecast every week, starting immediately.
3. [Optional: add any scheduling, overtime or labor-cost experience you already have.]

My work so far has already helped the payroll: shorter training and lower turnover both cut labor costs. The budget is the next step, and I'm ready for it.

**My request**
Please appoint me Front Office Manager. I'd welcome a conversation about the role, the budget handover and what you'd want to see from me in the first 90 days.

[Your name]
</final_document>

Before Friday:
- Fill in the brackets.
- Delete the optional budget line if it doesn't apply to you.
- If you have numbers from your seven weeks in charge (occupancy, complaints, overtime), add one to that section. Real results from those weeks are your strongest evidence.
